The issuer, fixed monetary reference and contractual redemption scope are resolved; direct app redemption is not yet evidenced as live.

genius.notes: Reviewed 2026-10-15; restored after independent r1 adjudication. Binding terms resolve the exact legal issuer, the one-rand payment-token reference and the contractual redemption scope, so the assessment is retained rather than treating unresolved U.S. public posture as unresearched token identity. Authorization, issuer pathway, foreign exception, enforcement and DASP posture remain explicitly unknown; these are unresolved dimensions, not approval, unlawful-status or negative-enforcement findings. Scoped searches and accessible U.S. regulator material did not establish an exact issuer authorization/application record, but the OCC licensing response exposed metadata/navigation rather than a complete applications table. The prior complete-table negative-review claim could not be reproduced and is not refreshed. South African licensing and reserves do not establish U.S. permission. Current exchange exits have no issuer-guaranteed price, liquidity or settlement outcome; direct app redemption and its two-business-day promise apply only once launched. Public monthly AUP reports support disclosure-presence flags, not assurance: Moore expressly provides no assurance opinion or conclusion. The current archive has distinct monthly PDF links for November and December 2025 and January through August 2026; the old repeated-January-link caveat is obsolete. The latest publicly linked reserve snapshot remains August 31, 2026; this review does not refresh its balances. MiCA remains unassessed because a fixed-ZAR payment token does not qualify for the variable-NAV structural exclusion, and no high-confidence no-EU-offer or exact-token EU restriction evidence was established. The exact pre-review issuerEntity string is preserved to avoid an unintended Safety Score issuer-join change.
